source: Copernicus Sentinel-2 L2A true colour (TCI, 10 m), Earth Search STAC / AWS Open Data

period.summary: Rock-and-ice collapse at about 8:37 am Nepal time on 26 August 2026; the flood reached Betrawati at about 9:20 am. No end date in the sources used.

sources.says: Collapse at about 8:37 am (UTC+05:45) on the northern flank of the Langtang Lirung massif; flood at Betrawati at about 9:20 am.

searched: Sentinel-2 L2A scenes 10–29 August 2026 over the Betrawati–Gerkhu frame; published images and maps from ESA, the EU Space programme and UNOSAT
rule: Each stop shows only material from its own date. No image is used for two stops and nothing is drawn between them.

frame.heading: Before the flood
frame.sentence: The river runs in a narrow channel between Betrawati and Gerkhu.
frame.why: Clear Sentinel-2 image two weeks before the flood; the same frame as the Copernicus comparison.
frame.catalog: Earth Search STAC (AWS Open Data), collection sentinel-2-l2a

stages.title: About two hours after the collapse

frame.heading: About two hours after the collapse
frame.sentence: Landsat-9 took this image about two hours after the collapse. ESA used shortwave infrared, so ice and snow look bright blue.
frame.credit: Contains modified Landsat-9 data, processed by ESA
frame.why: ESA: acquired on 26 August, approximately two hours after the glacier had collapsed. Labels on the image are ESA's.
frame.product_id: Nepal glacier collapse and flood – before and after (31 Aug 2026)

frame.heading: The day after the flood
frame.sentence: Pale brown sediment now covers a much wider strip along the river, where on 12 August there was a narrow channel.
frame.why: First clear Sentinel-2 image after the flood (91 % clear in the frame; cloud in the east).
frame.catalog: Earth Search STAC (AWS Open Data), collection sentinel-2-l2a

frame.heading: Lake overflow
frame.sentence: The UNOSAT map shows where the two lakes are; the overflow is known from a news report (Reuters).
frame.note: The map shows where the lakes are. The overflow comes from the news report, not from the map.
frame.why: Lake outlines from UNOSAT (about 12 ha and 19 ha; preliminary, not validated in the field). Background map: not from 28 August.

extra_note: Checked 2026-11-12 for captures of the same frame between the main stops (12–28 Aug): Sentinel-2 17 and 22 Aug 100 % cloud, 24 Aug 81 % cloud; Landsat-8 18 Aug shows the same pre-flood state as 12 Aug with cloud over Betrawati; Landsat-9 26 Aug 04:48 UTC (10:33 Nepal time) 70 % cirrus and 87 % cloud or shadow, valley not readable. None added.
